what_happened: The person running Athena merged pull request #673 by hand on GitHub, around `athena land`. The required history check then failed on every later pull request, because the merge had no landing intent on the records branch. With Sri's approval, the the person running Athena wrote landing intents on athena/records for #673 (merge commit da1ab58) and #675. They committed with --no-verify, as Athena's records writer does. The first ids used invalid letters, so a follow-up commit renamed them. Reconcile then wrote landing record 20261116-155711-sr9v. This is a hand repair of the records after the earlier hand merge.
cause: Athena has no supported way to adopt a pull request that was merged outside `athena land`. The history check requires a landing intent for each merge, and only the land path writes one. So when a drain ends before merging a green pull request and the the person running Athena merges it by hand, the check fails for all later pull requests. The only fix is to hand-write records, and the writer's id format is not enforced or documented where the the person running Athena works, so the first ids were invalid.
other_causes: The drain ended before merging a green pull request, which pushed the the person running Athena to merge by hand (see earlier case 20261116-125744-f4nk).
Landing-intent id rules are not validated before commit, and --no-verify skips the hooks, so bad ids were caught only later.
The the person running Athena imitates the records writer by hand, with no command that does it.
open_hypotheses: Whether #675 was also merged by hand or only needed an intent because of the #673 gap; the fields do not say.
Whether the first invalid ids were rejected by a check or noticed by the the person running Athena; the fields do not say.
prevention: Add an `athena adopt-merge <pr>` command, or make reconcile do it automatically. It would detect a pull request merged outside `athena land` and write a valid landing intent on the records branch, with correctly formed ids and no hand --no-verify commit. It would also have the history check name this exact fix in its refusal message. Separately, a drain should not end while a green pull request is unmerged. That keeps the the person running Athena from merging by hand in the first place.
proposed_request: Add an `athena adopt-merge <pr-number>` command, which reconcile also runs automatically. When a pull request has been merged on GitHub outside `athena land`, the command writes a landing intent for it on athena/records using the same records writer and id generator that `athena land` uses. It must refuse invalid ids and must be safe to run twice. Acceptance: (1) In a test, a hand-merged pull request produces a valid landing intent, and reconcile then writes the landing record. (2) The required history check passes for the next pull request after that. (3) Running it twice writes nothing new. (4) When the history check refuses because a merge has no intent, its message names `athena adopt-merge`. (5) Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
